headline: Geopolitical Fog Hangs Over the Open as Oil Surges and Rate-Hike Fears Spread
body_html:
Futures traders are navigating a charged pre-market landscape this Monday morning, carrying momentum from a broadly positive Friday session into a week defined by two looming macro forces: escalating Middle East tensions and the growing likelihood of coordinated rate increases across G7 central banks. Friday's close saw 395 of 545 tracked names advance, with semiconductors leading all sectors higher by 3.15%, while homebuilders and industrials also posted solid gains. Healthcare was the lone sector in the red, slipping fractionally.

Crude oil is the flashpoint heading into the open. Prices surged nearly 3% on fresh strikes targeting Saudi infrastructure and renewed anxiety over the Strait of Hormuz, where a proposed diplomatic meeting has now been postponed. AirBaltic's Chapter 11 filing — attributed in part to the economic fallout from the Iran conflict — underscores that war costs are beginning to reach balance sheets beyond the energy patch. The Houthis' advance in Yemen is adding further pressure on Gulf-state stability.

On the policy front, all eyes are reportedly fixed on Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh as rate-hike expectations build across the G7. Separately, Anthropic's latest AI safety warning is drawing scrutiny toward chip-sector valuations, even as the broader semiconductor trade remains intact. Watch energy and industrials closely at the bell.

briefs.headline: Oil Extends Rally After Strikes on Saudi Infrastructure and Hormuz Tension
briefs.body: Crude prices climbed nearly 3% Friday after new strikes targeted Saudi energy facilities and anxiety mounted over the Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor. A planned diplomatic gathering of Gulf states and Iran in Oman has been postponed, removing a near-term de-escalation catalyst and leaving energy markets exposed to further upside volatility at Monday's open.

briefs.headline: AirBaltic Seeks Chapter 11 Protection, Citing Iran-War Economic Fallout
briefs.body: European carrier AirBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, with the Iran conflict's ripple effects on aviation costs cited as a central factor. The filing signals that the economic damage from the Middle East confrontation is spreading beyond oil markets into consumer-facing industries, raising questions about additional casualties across global travel and logistics sectors.

briefs.headline: Warsh in Focus as G7 Rate-Hike Expectations Build
briefs.body: Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh is drawing intense market attention as a growing number of G7 central banks signal openness to rate increases. The synchronized hawkish tilt, if it materializes, could compress equity multiples heading into the autumn. Bond markets and rate-sensitive sectors such as homebuilders — which gained 1.58% Friday — will be closely monitored for early reactions.

briefs.headline: Anthropic AI Warning Raises Questions for Chip Sector Despite Intact Trade
briefs.body: A cautionary statement from Anthropic regarding artificial intelligence risks is generating pre-market discussion about semiconductor valuations. Analysts note the broader AI-driven chip trade appears structurally intact for now, but any sustained narrative around regulatory risk could temper enthusiasm. Semiconductors were the top-performing sector Friday, gaining 3.15% on the session.

briefs.headline: Vicor and Power-Linked Names Dominated Friday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: Power-module specialist Vicor Corporation surged 11.15% to lead all gainers Friday, joined by Forgent Power Solutions up 8.97% and ON Semiconductor advancing 8.51%. The cluster of power-technology names atop the leaderboard reflects sustained investor appetite for infrastructure plays tied to AI data-center electricity demand and grid modernization themes.

briefs.headline: Metallurgical Coal Stocks Slide as Materials Sector Lags
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal each shed 3.82% Friday, dragging the materials sector to one of its weakest showings in the session as metallurgical coal pricing faces headwinds. The paired declines stand in contrast to the broad market advance and may reflect softening steel-demand signals out of major industrial economies amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.
